prompt: Image 1 is one of our finished point-and-click adventure game backgrounds. Make exactly this local change: Remove the free-standing wooden caretaker's desk on the left of the back wall (below the key cabinet, in front of the lower half of the plain single wooden door) together with everything on it - the green desk lamp, the open book and the telephone - and its shadow and its reflection on the floor. Where it stood, continue exactly what is behind it: the lower part of that single door with its brown frame down to the floor, the yellow wall with the darker yellow-ochre dado, the diagonal bands of sunlight on the wall, the brown skirting board and the polished terrazzo floor with the same tile joints, sun patches and reflections; nothing stands on the floor there. Add one small new object instead: a small wall-mounted wooden lectern for the visitor book, on the yellow wall just right of that single door's frame (its left edge about a hand's width right of the frame, well left of the middle double door): a narrow slanted wooden board about half as wide as the door, fixed directly to the wall on one triangular bracket, with no legs, its upper edge at the height of the door handle. An open visitor book with illegible scribbled handwriting lies on the slanted board, and a pen on a short string hangs beside it. Do not change the key cabinet, the doors, the clock or anything else. Change nothing else: keep every other object, the camera, the composition, all positions, sizes, colours and the light exactly as in image 1. No people, no animals, no text, no logos, no frames. Image 2 is another background from the same game: keep the same painting technique. Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
